C_selected_realization.setup: m odd, q|C, q does not divide A,B,D,P,M,Q; write kappa=q*kappa0
C_selected_realization.coordinate: choose theta^2=A/B in Q_q and put t=theta*x
C_selected_realization.plus_pair: both plus radicands are q-units and squares near x=+/-1 by the second AE input; AB is a square so the extra plus root has the same character
C_selected_realization.m_at_least_3_construction: take x=epsilon+q*c with c a q-unit chosen so Legendre(kappa0*A*(-2*epsilon*c),q)=+1. Since 1<m, both minus factors have valuation 1 and the same normalized unit, so all four roots exist.
C_selected_realization.m_equal_1_reduction: write s=kappa0*A and ell=(lambda^2-1)/q. For x=epsilon+q*c put X=-2*epsilon*c. The two tied minus roots require Legendre(s*X,q)=Legendre(s*(X-ell),q)=+1. For x=epsilon+q^n*c with odd n>=3, the extra-minus condition is Legendre(-s*ell,q)=+1 while c can always satisfy the source-minus condition.
C_selected_realization.finite_field_count: let a=Legendre(s*ell,q). The number of nonzero X, X-ell with both required same character is (q-3-a*(1+Legendre(-1,q)))/4.
C_selected_realization.consequence: for every odd q>=5 at least the n=1 or the n>=3 construction works. For q=3 the branch is locally impossible exactly when Legendre(s*ell,3)=+1; it is realizable when that symbol is -1.
C_selected_realization.q3_integer_criterion: because M^2 is a square unit, the q=3 failure condition is Legendre((kappa/3)*A*8*(D0/3),3)=+1 when v_3(D0)=1 and 3|C

D_selected_realization.setup: m odd, q|D, q does not divide A,B,C,P,M,Q; write rho=q*rho0
D_selected_realization.coordinate: choose theta^2=-A/B in Q_q and put t=theta*x
D_selected_realization.untied_minus_comparison: near x=+/-1 the source minus root is a q-unit square by the second AE input, while the extra minus radicand differs in character by A*B. Hence simultaneous source/extra minus roots require Legendre(A*B,q)=+1.
D_selected_realization.branch_only_condition: combining Legendre(A*B,q)=+1 with the AE input Legendre(-A*B,q)=+1 gives Legendre(-1,q)=+1, equivalently q congruent 1 modulo 4
D_selected_realization.sufficiency: when q=1 mod4, AB is a square and the tied plus pair reduces to the same-character problem as the C-selected case. For m>=3 the x=epsilon+q*c construction works; for m=1, q>=5 and the finite-field/n>=3 alternatives are exhaustive, so a construction always exists.
